text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Jordan to present 25 investment plans in industry, transport, water, tourism and energy sectors at Cairo Middle East economic summit. Tourism projects to include plans for 37,000 tourist beds in Aqaba and Dead Sea resorts.
- Fouad Hussein, head of journalists' freedoms committee, released on 20,000 dinar ($28,200) bail by state security court.
- Prime Minister Kabariti says government determined to put stop to football violence.
- Kabariti meets PLO official Husseini, says Jordan committed to its Palestinian brothers. Husseini says Israel trying to change Hebron deal.
- King Hussein phones Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Palestinian Authority President Arafat to stress need to carry out Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron.
- Jordanian opposition groups travel to Damascus to express solidarity with Syria over stalled peace talks with Israel.
- State sector pharmacists consider memorandum of understanding with government not binding, demand 120 percent allowances.
- Ministry of Supply delays issuing ration cards for 1997, considers cancelling ration cards next year, replacing it with single payment to needy people.
- International Monetary Fund study shows that inflation in Tunis, Jordan and Morocco is lowest in region. Customs tariffs in Jordan and Israel also low.
- King Hussein meets head of U.S. Central Command Lieutenant-General Binford Peay to discuss defence ties.
